1. Passkeys are a trap

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

Critics are arguing that passkeys, touted as the future of authentication, present significant security and usability risks. The primary concern is that they lock users into specific ecosystems, making account recovery difficult and centralized control inevitable.

My Take

Passkeys are essentially the digital equivalent of a 'smart' lock that only works if your house is also owned by the lock manufacturer. It’s a classic tech pivot: replacing a password you can forget with a proprietary dependency you can’t escape. Remember, if you don't own your keys, you're just a tenant in your own account.

5. Fingerprints are the new cookies

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

Browser fingerprinting is increasingly replacing traditional cookies as the primary method for tracking users across the web. This technique uses unique hardware and software configurations to identify individuals without needing to store data on their devices.

My Take

Cookies were the annoying houseguests who left crumbs everywhere; browser fingerprinting is the private investigator standing outside your window taking notes on your shoes. We’ve traded 'privacy-invading snacks' for 'unavoidable biological-digital signatures.' If you think you're anonymous online, you're just not being tracked hard enough yet.

Summary

My Take
